newsitem.title: REPUBLIC OF IRELAND: SOCCER-IRELAND CONFIDENT OF GETTING BACK ON TRACK.
newsitem.headline: SOCCER-IRELAND CONFIDENT OF GETTING BACK ON TRACK.

text.p: Ireland are confident they can get their World Cup group eight qualifying campaign back on track with a victory over Liechtenstein at Lansdowne Road on Wednesday (kick-off 1830 GMT).
"We can win all of our remaining games, starting with Liechtenstein, and still qualify for the World Cup finals next summer through the play-offs," manager Mick McCarthy said.

Ireland, who drew at 0-0 home to Iceland with Iceland and lost 3-2 in Macedonia and 1-0 in Romania nia (1-0) in their last three games, lie in fourth place in their six-team group with seven points from five matches.
Romania top the group with maximum points from six games. Macedonia are second with 10 points from six matches while Lithuania are third on nine points from five.
McCarthy gave clues as to his likely game plan on Wednesday when Ireland played Celtic in Dublin at the weekend.

In the defeat by Romania last month, Ireland played a 4-5-1 formation with Leeds United's Gary Kelly and Mark Kennedy of Liverpool playing deep on the wings and Watford's David Connolly operating as the sole striker.
Ireland again lined-up in a 4-5-1 set-up on Sunday, but this time both Kelly and Kennedy stayed forward far more.
Kennedy left the field in the second-half against Celtic with a recurrence of a groin injury but he trained with the Ireland squad on Tuesday and he is expected to play.

Watford striker David Connolly, who has missed five of Ireland's last six internationals due to injuries, was chosen at centre-forward for Sunday's match but he withdrew just before kick-off because he felt a thigh start to tighten.
Connolly trained with Ireland on Tuesday and it is expected he will be fit to play on Wednesday.
Liechtenstein prop up group eight after six successive defeats and a goal tally of 2-31.
Ireland beat them 5-0 in Liechtenstein last August, and should equal that total at least on Wednesday.
Alfred Riedl, who took over as manager in February, is more hopeful than expectant of seeing a repeat of the scoreless draw Liechtenstein recorded at home to the Irish in June 1995.
"We are the weakest team in the group. We just hope not to lose by a high score. If we fight and work, maybe we can have a chance on the counter-attack," Riedl said.
The only professional footballer in Liechtenstein's 22-man squad is Mario Frick of FC Basel in Switzerland. He missed the 2-0 home defeat by Lithuania last month because of injury.
It is expected that Frick will captain the visitors from a midfield position.

Meanwhile Ireland will be watched by a distinguished visitor on Wednesday -- their former manager Jack Charlton, who will see the team play for the first time since he resigned as manager after Ireland lost to the Netherlands in the Euro 96 playoff at Liverpool in December 1995.
Lineups:
Ireland (probable): Shay Given; Jeff Kenna, Ken Cunningham, Ian Harte, Steve Staunton; Gary Kelly, Ray Houghton, Roy Keane, Andy Townsend, Mark Kennedy; David Connolly.

Liechtenstein (from): Martin Oehry, Martin Heeb, Martin Brunhart; Thomas Hanselmann, Patrick Hefti, Jurgen Ospelt, Martin Stocklasa, Daniel Telser, Thomas Verling, Patrik Marxer; Ralf Ackermann; Christoph Frick, Daniel Hasler, Peter Klaunzer, Alexander Schadler, Rolf Sele, Martin Telser, Daniel Frick, Franz Schadler, Harry Zech, Mario Frick, Herbert Bicker.
